extracted.intended_audience: Recipients of Federal education funding (K-12 and postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, school administrators, and legal counsel responsible for Title IX compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Interpretation and implementation guidance for Title IX regulatory requirements addressing preemption, Title IX Coordinator designation and duties, nondiscrimination policies, grievance procedures, and notices for recipients of Federal education funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preemption of conflicting State or local law
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.6(b) preempts any State or local law or other requirement 'that conflicts with Title IX or this part.' The Department removed the prior 'greater protections' language and narrowed the focus to conflicts with Title IX or the implementing regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department will offer technical assistance, as appropriate, to promote compliance but will not provide opinions about how the regulations apply to specific facts or specific State and local laws without first conducting an investigation. Example: a State law that requires a recipient to discriminate on the basis of sexual orientation or gender identity would create a conflict and be preempted. Preemption is limited to conflicts (see conflict preemption standard) and does not extend beyond the Department's authority to effectuate Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict preemption standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Under conflict preemption, a federal regulation implicitly overrides state law when state law is in actual conflict with federal law either because it is impossible for a private party to comply with both state and federal requirements or because state law stands as an obstacle to the accomplishment and execution of the full purposes and objectives of Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department cites Supreme Court and circuit precedent that agencies acting within congressionally delegated authority may preempt state regulation. Preemption can arise from federal statutes or regulations when the conflict test is met (impossibility or obstacle to federal objectives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of constitutional rights (Due Process and First Amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections §106.6(d)(1)-(3) make clear nothing in the Title IX regulations requires a recipient to deprive a person of rights protected under the Due Process Clauses of the Fifth and Fourteenth Amendments or to restrict rights guaranteed by the First Amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations should not be interpreted to suppress protected speech by public or private recipients. Nothing in Title IX or this part would preempt a State law that safeguards speech protected by the First Amendment. However, a conflicting State law governing speech unprotected by the U.S. Constitution would not relieve the recipient's obligation to comply with Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient ultimate responsibility for compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient itself is responsible for compliance with obligations under Title IX, including any responsibilities assigned to the recipient's Title IX Coordinator under the final regulations; Title IX and regulations apply to 'every recipient and to all sex discrimination occurring under a recipient's education program or activity in the United States.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The designation of a Title IX Coordinator does not shift legal responsibility from the recipient to the individual; the recipient remains ultimately accountable. Recipients retain ability to address discrimination in ways that do not conflict with the final regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of a Title IX Coordinator
rubrics_metrics.description: Section §106.8(a)(1) requires each recipient to designate 'a' Title IX Coordinator (not necessarily 'the'); a recipient may designate more than one employee to serve as Title IX Coordinator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a recipient has more than one Title IX Coordinator, the recipient must designate one to retain 'ultimate oversight' and 'ensure the recipient's consistent compliance' with Title IX. The Title IX Coordinator must be authorized to coordinate the recipient's efforts to comply with Title IX and this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation and use of designees for Title IX duties
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may delegate, or permit a Title IX Coordinator to delegate, specific duties to one or more designees under §106.8(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegation decisions are recipient- and fact-specific and depend on factors like enrollment size, number of employees, locations, and variety of activities. Oversight does not require a supervisory relationship. Use of designees can assign duties to those best positioned to perform them, avoid conflicts of interest, and align with administrative structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Title IX Coordinator contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Section §106.8(c)(1)(i)(C) requires a recipient to publish the name or title, office address, email address, and telephone number of the recipient's Title IX Coordinator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing in the final regulations prevents a recipient from publicizing contact information for other persons appointed to coordinate compliance. Ensuring community members can identify and contact the Title IX Coordinator is important for awareness and safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt, publish, and implement nondiscrimination policy and grievance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must adopt, publish, and implement nondiscrimination policies, grievance procedures, and a notice of nondiscrimination to ensure students and others are protected from sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department added 'implement' (§106.8(b)(1) and (2)) to emphasize a recipient must actually carry out policies and procedures, not merely adopt them. The Department requires one grievance procedure (one or a set of procedures consistent with §106.45, and if applicable §106.46) with additional requirements related to sex-based harassment complaints involving a student at a postsecondary institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedures scope and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's grievance procedures apply to complaints alleging any action prohibited by Title IX 'or' this part and apply to complaints made by students, employees, or other individuals participating or attempting to participate in the recipient's education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The term 'other individuals' replaces 'third parties' to clarify scope. A complainant is not required to exhaust administrative remedies with the recipient before filing a complaint with the Office for Civil Rights (OCR). Grievance procedures must be publicized and consistent with the regulatory requirements in §106.45 (and §106.46 where applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of nondiscrimination content and concision
rubrics_metrics.description: Section §106.8(c)(1) requires the notice of nondiscrimination to notify individuals of rights protected by Title IX and how to make a report or complaint under Title IX, and the notice must be published in accordance with §106.8(c)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department favors a concise and accessible notice and therefore declines to require listing rights under State or local laws or proof of training in the notice. The notice should include how to locate the recipient's nondiscrimination policy and grievance procedures (consolidated into §106.8(c)(1)(i)(D)). Recipients may, but are not required to, enumerate additional bases (e.g., pregnancy, parental status, gender identity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'attempting to participate' (breadth of coverage)
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations use the term 'attempting to participate' (rather than 'applying') to describe individuals covered by grievance procedures and notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Attempting to participate' better encompasses broad circumstances (e.g., persons who applied or withdrew but would re-enroll if the recipient appropriately responds to allegations) and avoids inappropriately narrowing coverage to just 'applying.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Department technical assistance versus case-specific opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will offer technical assistance, as appropriate, to promote compliance with the final regulations, but will refrain from offering opinions about how the regulations apply to specific facts or specific State and local laws without first conducting an investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients seeking application of the regulations to particular factual scenarios should expect the Department to conduct an investigation before issuing an opinion; technical assistance will be available for general compliance questions.
